- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and prices are falling, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak for next 7–14 days.  
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.33 to -0.00 or vice versa), model lags by 1–3 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead or backward depending on sentiment direction.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67); model often overreacts; dampen forecast by 0.5–1.5% for 10–20 days after sentiment stabilizes.  
- In high-sentiment periods, model tends to ignore recent low prices; force a 1–2 day lag in price correction to align with sentiment decay.
